summary: A note whose title contains an ampersand can be opened again, and the gate can tell how old her position is.
details: Every index escapes what it renders, so a note called 'Dinner & drinks' reached her as 'Dinner &amp; drinks' — and the tools told her to type the title back exactly as shown, then refused it because the stored title has no entity in it. The handle now unescapes before comparing, in the one place all three readers share.
That refusal cost more than a retry: a proactive reminder written without its note id falls through to the flag-only screen, so the cancellation that fires when a note has moved on never runs.

The Relevance Gate's standing block now carries how long ago it was folded. Its instruction leans on that block as the only thing that can establish something she owes a room, and asks whether the room has already moved past a thread — both questions about when, decided against a paragraph with no time on it.
limitations: Nothing measures the gate's standing age yet: the suite's case format has no way to say how old a position is.
One audit finding was checked and rejected: the participation instrument promises a distance figure, and the location tool does return one on every trip.
